clue.text: The black monk is drunk

definitions.meaning: a monk of the order of St Benedict, whose habit is black
here a noun-like sense: a thing that is drunk, namely the herbal liqueur made at Fécamp

explanation.definitionFit: The order founded by St Benedict wears black habits, and its name also labels a French herbal liqueur sipped after dinner.

clue.text: Avifauna doing a stretch the maximum

parts.note: a stretch is a prison term, which in slang is bird (from rhyming slang bird-lime, time)
life imprisonment is the maximum sentence a court can hand down

explanation.surface: Someone serving the longest possible prison term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doing a stretch the maximum' paints a convict serving a life sentence; 'doing' is only a link. BIRD is British slang for a spell in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Avifauna is the collective term for the birds of a region, its feathered wildlife.

clue.text: Ties isthmus to river

parts.note: a neck of land is a narrow strip joining two larger masses, like an isthmus
the Wear is a river in north-east England flowing through Durham and Sunderland

explanation.surface: Someone tying a narrow strip of land to a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ties' reads as a verb but is the plural noun: neckties. The Wear is a river in County Durham, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Ties and cravats are worn round the throat, so they fall under the clothing category of things worn at the collar.

clue.text: It takes steam out of Derry

indicators.note: out of signals that the letters of Derry are knocked out of their order and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Something drawing vapour away from the Northern Irish city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of' looks like part of the definition (a machine that takes steam out of things) but it is the anagram signal working on DERRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A clothes or tumble dryer works by driving off moisture, carrying away the steam from wet laundry.

clue.text: Don't talk to a girl, it could hurt

parts.note: to cut someone is to snub them, refusing to speak to them
lass is a northern British and Scottish word for a girl

explanation.surface: Advice to a shy person: avoid speaking to a girl or it may end in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it could hurt' is the definition: a cutlass is a weapon. To 'cut' someone is to ignore them deliberately.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutlass is a short curved sword favoured by sailors, a weapon able to wound.

clue.text: I am in the loch and up the creek

indicators.note: in puts the word am inside the name of the Scottish loch

parts.note: Loch Ness is the famous Scottish loch
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stranded in a Scottish lake and in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts AM inside the loch's name; the I before it stands alone. 'the loch' here is Loch Ness in the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Being up the creek is an idiom for being in serious trouble or a muddle.

clue.text: Poles operate changed language

indicators.note: changed tells the solver to rearrange the gathered letters into something new

parts.note: the two poles are north and south, N and S

explanation.surface: Polish people running something in a modified tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' suggests people from Poland but gives N and S, the two magnetic poles; these join OPERATE and 'changed' reorders all nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Esperanto is the constructed international tongue devised by Zamenhof in 1887.

clue.text: See 13
The rockrose has feminine relations, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is spoken, and the answer matches its sound

parts.note: sisters are female relatives

explanation.surface: A flower that has female family members, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, SISTERS sounds close to CISTUS, the botanical name of the rockrose.
explanation.definitionFit: Cistus is the genus of Mediterranean shrubs commonly called rock roses.

clue.text: An assertion that reveals he nationalised the canal

indicators.note: that reveals signals the name is uncovered inside the run of the words that come before

explanation.surface: A claim that exposes the man who took over the Suez Canal.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'aN ASSERtion'. Gamal Abdel Nasser, Egypt's president, nationalised the Suez Canal in 1956.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasser seized the Suez Canal Company for Egypt in 1956, provoking the Suez Crisis.

clue.text: Mounts likely to fall?

parts.note: read as unsteady and liable to topple, while 'Mounts' hints at the North American mountain range with this name

explanation.surface: Horses or hills on the point of toppling over.
explanation.walkthrough: The word means wobbly, apt to fall, and the Rockies are mountains: a mount full of rocks could also be described this way.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shaky or unstable is liable to topple, like an unsteady mountain.

clue.text: The white monks won't talk

definitions.meaning: Cistercians of the Strict Observance, who wear white habits
describes those members of the order famed for keeping silence

explanation.definitionFit: The order founded at La Trappe wears white and is known for its rule of silence, so its members do not speak.

clue.text: Cow holder in which are clues but not solutions

definitions.text: in which are clues but not solutions

parts.note: a cow lows, so it is a 'lower', one that lows
a case is a container or holder

explanation.surface: A pen for cattle, then a remark on how crosswords are printed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cow' is not the verb to intimidate: a cow lows, so it is a LOWER. Crossword clues are printed in small letters, the solutions in capitals.
explanation.definitionFit: Small letters, as opposed to capitals, are the style in which clues are printed while grid entries use capitals.

clue.text: See 23
Grey friar was manager in football club I examine

indicators.note: in puts the piece for being in charge inside the club abbreviation

parts.note: ran means managed, was in charge of
to scan is to examine closely

explanation.surface: A friar who once managed a football club, and an inspector.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal. The Franciscans were called Grey Friars in England from the colour of their habits.
explanation.definitionFit: Followers of St Francis of Assisi were known in England as Grey Friars from their grey habits.

clue.text: Money and a true corrupter, drink

parts.note: a coin is a piece of money

indicators.note: a corrupter spoils or perverts, so the letters of 'a true' are perverted into a new order

explanation.surface: Cash and a genuine source of moral decay, as a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupter' looks like a noun describing the drink, but it is the anagram signal working on the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cointreau is a French orange-flavoured liqueur, a drink.

clue.text: George takes part of theatre as play area

parts.note: George Sand was the pen name of the French novelist Aurore Dupin
the pit is the area in front of the stage, for orchestra or cheap seats

explanation.surface: A man named George takes a section of the playhouse as his stage.
explanation.walkthrough: George Sand was the nineteenth-century French novelist; the pit is a section of a theatre. 'Play' hints at drama but the definition is a children's play space.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandpit is a shallow box of sand where children can dig and play.

clue.text: Witty 'graphic and strangely boring occupation

indicators.note: strangely says the gathered letters appear in an odd new order

parts.note: the fodder as meant is Witty 'n' graphic and, the 'n'' (short for 'and') giving an N that the held clue lost

explanation.surface: A witty and vivid but odd way of describing a dull pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: All sixteen letters of WITTY, N, GRAPHIC and AND are rearranged, 'strangely' signalling the anagram. The clue as held lacks the 'n'' (shown by the stray apostrophe) that gives the needed N.
explanation.definitionFit: Watching paint dry is the proverbial example of something tediously dull to do.

clue.text: See 16
Reliable business

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective sense is steady and dependable; the noun sense is a commercial company or partnership.

clue.text: Diaphragm used in the course of a repeated musical phrase

parts.note: mid is a short form of amid, meaning during or in the middle of
a riff is a short repeated phrase in jazz or rock

explanation.surface: A breathing muscle employed while playing a recurring tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diaphragm' is not here the muscle itself: it stands for the body area around it, the middle of the torso.
explanation.definitionFit: The midriff is the middle part of the body, and the term is also used for the diaphragm muscle in that region.

clue.text: Going by the same rate, a parrot is sick

indicators.note: a sick parrot is out of sorts, so its letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Charged at an equal rate, a parrot feels unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of A PARROT, signalled by 'sick', gives the Latin phrase meaning in proportion.
explanation.definitionFit: Pro rata is Latin for 'in proportion', describing charges at an equal proportional rate.

clue.text: Religious leader about a mile — two-from buried city

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the leader goes round the mile

parts.note: the Pope is the head of the Roman Catholic Church
M is the abbreviation for mile
II is two in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A priest some distance from a city lost under ash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal; the dash is punctuation only. Pompeii was buried by the eruption of Vesuvius in AD 79.
explanation.definitionFit: Pompeii was the Roman town smothered in volcanic ash when Vesuvius erupted.

clue.text: Ipecacuanha dissolved? It never does

indicators.note: dissolved means broken down and its parts mixed into a new arrangement

parts.note: ipecac is the usual short name for ipecacuanha, the emetic drug

explanation.surface: A medicine that has been dissolved, though something never melts.
explanation.walkthrough: IPECAC, the standard short form of the drug's name, is rearranged. 'It never does' refers back to 'dissolved': a polar ice sheet ideally never melts.
explanation.definitionFit: A polar ice sheet is a mass of permanent ice that should never melt away.

clue.text: Incentive for a vehicle? Nonsense!

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
rot is nonsense, rubbish talk

explanation.surface: An inducement to buy a car dismissed as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: A carrot is the reward dangled in front of a donkey to make it move, hence an incentive.
explanation.definitionFit: The figurative carrot is a reward offered to encourage effort, as opposed to the stick.

clue.text: Yellow and green monks' plan to recycle?

definitions.note: the monks' product here is a liqueur in yellow and green varieties

parts.note: a chart is a map or plan
to reuse is to use again, to recycle

explanation.surface: Coloured monks drawing up a scheme for recycling.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is elliptical: the yellow and green liqueur made by the Carthusian monks near Grenoble.
explanation.definitionFit: The Carthusian monks distil a herbal liqueur sold in green and yellow forms.

clue.text: Black friar's party: a little one has power

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
a mini is a small version of something, a little one
can means is able, has the power to

explanation.surface: A friar dressed in black throws a party where a small person has influence.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dominicans were called Black Friars from the black cloaks over their white habits.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Order of Preachers founded by St Dominic were known as Black Friars from their cloaks.

clue.text: The Asian pear, a tree found in Ulster

indicators.note: found in means the tree is placed within the province's abbreviation

parts.note: Ulster is commonly used for Northern Ireland, abbreviated NI
the ash is a tree

explanation.surface: A fruit, and a tree growing in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' is the container signal. Ulster, strictly a historic province, is commonly used to mean Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The nashi is a crisp, round pear from East Asia, also called the apple pear.

clue.text: White friar makes Conservative supply top people with weapons

parts.note: to supply with weapons is to arm, and top people are the elite, so the phrase is arm elite

explanation.surface: A friar wearing white gets a Tory to equip the upper class with arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply ... with weapons' wraps round 'top people' in the clue, reading as ARM followed by ELITE. The Carmelites were called White Friars from their white mantles.
explanation.definitionFit: The Carmelite friars wore white cloaks, so in England they were known as White Friars.

clue.text: Jumped high in the air from the snow?

definitions.meaning: a ball hit high into the air is said to have been sent up skyward in this way
a skier comes down from the snow slopes, so a whimsical past tense of ski

explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a ball hit steeply upward is skyed this way, and the same letters are the past tense of the verb to ski on snow.

clue.text: See 15
Repulsive round in final upheaval every single time

indicators.note: round means the repulsive word goes round the shuffled letters

parts.note: ugly means repulsive to look at

indicators.note: an upheaval turns things over, so in and final are jumbled

explanation.surface: A nasty round of shake-ups at the end, happening every time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upheaval' is the anagram signal on 'in final', and 'round' has the word for repulsive wrapped round the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfailingly means without exception, on every occasion.
